business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — US-derived common law (Business Corporations Act modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law and New York Business Corporation Law) with customary law elements applicable to land and domestic matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the United States of America and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986, as amended in 2003)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus, 2019)
Intergovernmental Agreement between the United States and the Republic of the Marshall Islands for Cooperation in International Taxation (FATCA Model 1A IGA, 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, as amended ('AML/CFT Act'); Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2018/2022 as promulgated by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; Business Corporations Act, 48 MIRC Chapter 1, as amended ('RMI BCA'); Registrar of Corporations Beneficial Ownership Directions 2023; Insurance Act 2001, as amended, and Insurance Regulations 2002; Criminal Code 2003 (money laundering and financing of terrorism predicate offenses)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of UBO passport (identity and nationality pages) and residential address proof
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of origin; passport issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain — notarization in the origin country, Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, then legalization at the RMI diplomatic/consular post (RMI is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Clearance / Name Reservation Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization by the RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (for overseas corporate-parent and banking counterparts)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO Declaration, PEP Self-Certification and Personal History Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Marshall Islands notary public / Commissioner of Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain — RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, then destination-country consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent AML/CFT Onboarding Acknowledgment and UBO Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization via RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (where required by foreign AML/CFT counterparties)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, MIRC Title 51, as amended (sections governing incorporation, registered office, and first board action: Sections 34-56, 64, and 68)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Association Section, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (executed in duplicate, with Consent of Registered Agent appended)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement and no escrow account mandate; the authorized capital stated in the Articles is fully at the discretion of the incorporator, with shares issuable for lawful consideration as determined by the Board
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporator's subscription for the initial authorized share capital and the issuance of shares to the sole shareholder be, and hereby are, ratified and accepted; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, as designated by the Registered Agent, be adopted as the statutory registered office and the Registered Agent be retained for ongoing statutory filings; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Corporation's Bylaws as presented to this Board be adopted in their entirety; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until successors are duly elected; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers be authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and take all actions necessary to obtain the marine survey operating license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Association Section, Office of the Attorney General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name reservation request listing the proposed corporate name and three alternates, together with the reservation fee. The name must be distinguishable from all registered entities and must not imply a governmental affiliation. The reservation certificate, valid for a stated administrative period, must be attached to the Articles of Incorporation at filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for conflict or prohibited wording, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar within 10 days or immediately amend the application with an alternate name; the reservation fee is applied to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (legalization chain where applicable); filing review by the Office of the Attorney General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English stating the corporate name, registered agent's name and address, authorized share structure, purpose clause encompassing marine claims inspection and survey services, and the liability limitation election. Each incorporator must execute the Articles before a Notary Public; the Registered Agent must execute the Consent to Appointment. Where executed outside the Marshall Islands, the notarial signature must be authenticated by apostille under the Hague Convention.
required_dossiers: Consent to Appointment of Registered Agent
Due diligence questionnaire of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query deficiency notice, the filer must amend the defective clause and re-file within 14 business days; administrative deficiencies are curable by letter from counsel without loss of filing priority if addressed within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Association Section, Office of the Attorney General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation, Consent of Registered Agent, and Name Reservation Certificate to the Registrar together with the statutory filing fee. Payment is made by bank wire or certified check to the Office of the Attorney General. Upon compliance review, the Registrar endorses and files the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is the conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
required_dossiers: Filed Articles of Incorporation with Registrar stamp
Consent to Appointment of Registered Agent (filed)
Certificate of Designation of Registered Office (if separate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is withheld due to fee dispute or incomplete dossiers, the applicant must reconcile the fee ledger with the Treasury and submit the missing instrument; expedited administrative review is available upon written request with supporting proof of compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting: Bylaws Adoption, Officer Appointments, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors or act by unanimous written consent. The board adopts the corporate Bylaws, approves the form of share certificate, accepts the Incorporator's subscription, issues share certificates to the shareholder, appoints the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, and authorizes opening bank accounts and executing contracts.
required_dossiers: Notice or Waiver of Notice of First Board Meeting
Minutes of First Board Meeting or Unanimous Written Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director is unavailable to execute the consent, the appointment may be deferred by board resolution and ratified at the next meeting; no statutory filing is required for this internal action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registrations and License Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations; Ministry of Finance; Office of the Maritime Administrator (International Registries, Inc.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial corporate annual report notice with the Registrar, obtain the Tax Identification Number from the Ministry of Finance, and file the Foreign Investment Business License application (for non-resident ownership) together with the marine survey operating license application with the Office of the Maritime Administrator. These actions perfect the Corporation's standing to operate as a marine claims surveyor.
required_dossiers: Statement of non-resident ownership and corporate structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Foreign Investment Business License or maritime license is delayed, the Corporation may operate through a licensed local marine surveyor under a subcontracting arrangement and appeal any denial to the licensing authority within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Office of the Maritime Administrator, Republic of the Marshall Islands (administered through International Registries, Inc., in coordination with the Registrar of Foreign Investment)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Survey Services Operating License (Approved Marine Claims Surveyor Endorsement) and Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt – Category 3 (office-based professional surveying services with no industrial installation; no full EIA Report required unless operations expand to physical wreck dismantling or shore-based works)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated process wastewater or VOCs for office-only operations; any incidental waste must comply with EPA Solid Waste Management Regulations (40 CFR-equivalent standards in MIRC Title 25) and all ship-survey activities must follow the Marine Administrator's anti-pollution directives governing bilge water observation and fuel sampling; no hazardous waste generation without EPA permit
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.security_clearance_notes: Surveyor personnel assigned to board Class I foreign-flag vessels must hold valid marine surveyor credentials recognized by the Maritime Administrator; negative AML/CTF screening is required for all case-handling staff

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate from the Majuro Fire Department (sprinkler and egress compliance for office premises); Building Code structural load inspection certificate issued by the Majuro Land Management – Building Inspection Division for any survey workshop or equipment storage area; Occupational Health and Safety clearance confirming compliance with the Marshall Islands Workplace Safety Standards, including mandatory personal protective equipment (PPE) protocols for all harbor-side survey assignments and emergency evacuation plans approved by the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance, Revenue Division (Tax Administration and Collection); corporate registration administered by the Office of the Attorney General, Registrar of Corporations; official portal: www.rmi-finance.com and the Pacific Islands Electronic Corporate Registry (external service provider).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (RMI) is issued a Certificate of Incorporation bearing a statutory corporate registry number, which serves as the primary legal identifier. If the BC derives gross receipts sourced within the Republic, it must apply to the Revenue Division of the Ministry of Finance for a Gross Receipts Tax (GRT) registration, obtain a GRT taxpayer identification number, and file GRT returns. If the BC conducts no business within the RMI and has no RMI-source income, it may instead file a Non-Resident Domestic (NRD) election with the Registrar of Corporations, formalizing exemption from GRT. A Business Licence under the Business Licence Act is separately required before commencing any licensed marine surveying or insurance-adjacent activity within RMI territorial limits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch election exists. Available statutory elections under RMI law: (a) Non-Resident Domestic (NRD) election under Section 7 of the Business Corporations Act, effected by board resolution filed with the Registrar of Corporations and published, rendering all foreign-source income (including offshore marine survey fees) exempt from GRT; (b) affirmative GRT registration election for a BC that elects to conduct RMI-source business and be taxed on gross receipts at 3%; (c) election to operate as an exempt international shipping or marine-insurance auxiliary entity under the Insurance Act 2007 where survey fees derive from ocean-going vessels in international commerce; (d) no hybrid mismatch election is recognized, as the RMI has not adopted OECD hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The RMI imposes no VAT or GST. The closest indirect levies are the 3% Gross Receipts Tax (GRT) under the Revenue and Taxation Act 1999 and customs import duties under the RMI Customs Tariff Act 1993. GRT registration is mandatory from the first US dollar of gross receipts derived from business activity carried on within the Republic (no de minimis threshold); a wholly offshore marine surveyor with no RMI-source receipts has no GRT registration obligation. Import-duty registration applies only to importers of dutiable physical goods and is immaterial to export marine survey services. Functional currency: USD.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based invoice clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The RMI Customs Service operates an electronic customs declaration system for goods, but it does not serve as an indirect-tax invoice clearance mechanism. Marine surveyors issuing invoices to foreign underwriter clients retain paper or PDF invoices and are not subject to any fiscal digitalization mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: As the RMI imposes no VAT or GST, no VAT zero-rating claim is available or required. Under GRT law, income from marine insurance surveying, vessel hull and cargo damage inspection, and claims verification services falls outside the RMI tax base when (i) the services are physically performed outside RMI territorial waters or on board foreign-flag vessels in international transit, and (ii) consideration is paid by a non-resident underwriter or owner for offshore-sourced services. An NRD-elected BC achieves a structural de facto 0% rate; a GRT-registered BC may claim the territorial exclusion on its GRT return by allocating offshore gross receipts to extranational service categories. Substantiation requires service-performance location evidence (surveyor travel logs, vessel position records, interview/GPS data), non-resident counterparty identification, and the foreign-currency invoice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (RMI Cargo Export Entry; applicable where survey equipment or samples accompany the assignment, otherwise N/A for pure services)
Bill of Lading (vessel eBL or ocean carrier service contract evidencing international movement of the surveyed cargo or vessel)
Inward Remittance Certificate (USD wire creditor advice bearing the foreign drawer and matching the marine survey invoice reference)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Revenue Division may audit territorial allocations or NRD status under the Revenue and Taxation Act 1999 and the Business Corporations Act. Improper exclusion of RMI-source receipts is treated as under-reporting: failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalties accrue at 10% per month of the overdue tax, statutory interest runs on the balance, and a civil fraud penalty of 50% of the understated GRT may be imposed where false territorial certifications, fabricated survey logs, or fictitious Bills of Lading are produced. Criminal enforcement includes fines up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment for tax evasion; NRD status may be revoked retroactively upon proof of deception, the certificate of good standing is suspended, and all marine warranty-survey licensing renewals are blocked pending full clawback and penalty settlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No indigenous central bank; the official medium of exchange is the United States dollar under the Constitution of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Prudential banking and foreign-exchange-related supervision is vested in the Marshall Islands Banking Commission (under the Banking Act 1987, as amended), with day-to-day monitoring delegated to the Ministry of Finance and the Insurance and Pensions Regulator where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains a fully dollarized monetary system with no separate domestic legal tender and no exchange-control apparatus. Capital and current account transactions are freely convertible into United States dollars and foreign currencies through the licensed international banking network. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, liquidation proceeds, and royalty payments are not subject to central bank approval, exchange permits, or repatriation taxes at the treasury level. The jurisdiction accepts the convertibility obligations attendant to IMF Article VIII, and there are no statutory barriers to cross-border capital flows for a non-resident Business Corporation engaged in marine insurance claim surveying.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no prescribed repatriation timeline. Because the United States dollar is the domestic currency, proceeds earned in USD require no conversion and may be retained offshore or in local accounts at the entity's discretion. For any incidental foreign-currency receipts, the RMI does not impose a compulsory conversion; such funds may be held as foreign-currency deposits with licensed banks or converted via normal banking channels.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise or licensed cryptocurrency-fiat gateways may be used as auxiliary settlement rails for low-value marine survey disbursements, travel advances, and contractor payments. However, the RMI Banking Act imposes a statutory licensing requirement for deposit-taking institutions onshore; an unlicensed offshore EMI cannot lawfully hold escrow funds, provide a regulated capital account, or act as the primary correspondent for the marine insurance business. Legal constraints include the need to pass OFAC sanctions screening, beneficial ownership disclosure, and the risk that EMI-denominated virtual accounts may not be recognised as bank accounts for RMI statutory licensing and insurance-surveyor capitalisation purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring directors or beneficial owners to appear physically before an RMI bank. Remote account opening for non-resident Business Corporations is generally feasible where the corporate record is certified by the RMI Registrar of Corporations and accompanied by a notarised registered-agent certificate. In practice, Bank of Guam and Bank of Marshall Islands may require a secure video-conference interview, certified copies of passports, satisfactory beneficial-ownership attestation, and a banking reference from the respondent's home-country bank. A registered agent physically resident in Majuro is typically mandatory for statutory compliance and can assist with the documentary authentication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to nominees, protector appointors, or bearer shares in legacy structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate extract from the RMI Registrar; full chain of legal ownership, including declarations from any nominee shareholders and a nominee/agent undertaking to disclose beneficial owners; individual KYC documents for each natural person controlling the entity; and a legal opinion from an RMI-licensed corporate attorney confirming the entity is not a mere shell and carries active marine surveyor business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or premium inflow originating from high-risk maritime jurisdictions or cash-intensive freight operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed marine surveying contracts; vessel and cargo insurance policies; carrier bills of lading; invoice and payment-flow justification; source-of-funds statements from reinsurers or underwriting clients; confirmation of the RMI Business Corporation's statutory licence to provide ISIC 5222 surveying services; and documented corporate minutes authorising the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits related to vessel ownership, port calls, or trade counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel-screening report; International Maritime Organization registration or flag-state documentation; comprehensive OFAC/UN/UK sanctions lists check for all counterparties; voyage clearance and cargo documentation for the specific survey; certification that the survey is for post-loss inspection of insurance damage only and not for prohibited trade; an express compliance sign-off from the money laundering reporting officer or external counsel where derogatory hits are false positives.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or capital contributions to the non-resident Business Corporation may be routed by international SWIFT wire using MT103 for receipt of directly traceable premium-receivable-bearing funds or MT202 for interbank treasury transfers. Compliant practice is to include a payment purpose code consistent with the IMF Balance of Payments classification for direct investment and capital transfers (e.g., 'C3' equity investment or the relevant ISO 20022 'CAPC' supplementary code), together with a corporate resolution approving the equity injection and a certified board minute referencing the marine insurance surveyor business plan. Verification consists of matching the remitter with the corporate register, obtaining a bank debit confirmation from the sending institution, and retaining a source-of-capital statement from the shareholder where the funding exceeds repatriation thresholds. Because the RMI imposes no exchange controls, the wire will settle in USD without central bank approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for professional fees, survey overhead, contractor payments, reinsurance adjustments, and settlement of justified marine claim inspection costs should be effected via SWIFT MT103 (single-entry payment) or, for high-value and documentary transactions, along with ucp600-compliant commercial letters of credit (MT700). Funds clear in USD across the correspondent banking network using CHIPS and Fedwire within the US domestic clearing system. Where the payee is located outside the US, downstream clearing occurs via the payee bank's US correspondent. To preserve a clear audit trail, each outward MT103 should include an invoice reference, the contractual engagement ID, and a survey-report number.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward with a licensed international bank (non-NDF, due to full dollarization).
Cross-Currency Swap on USD against the payment currency.
FX Swap for temporary liquidity bridging between USD and foreign-currency receipts.
Vanilla FX Options for hedging receivables denominated in GBP, EUR, AUD, or other transactional currencies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations – Marshall Islands Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The last day of the calendar month in which the anniversary of incorporation occurs (e.g., 31 March for a March incorporation). Deadline is annual with no extension for non-resident entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% penalty per month (or fraction thereof) is added to the unpaid franchise tax up to a maximum of 50% of the tax due; continued default for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve or strike the company from the registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only for securities issuers registered with a stock exchange, licensed banks, insurers, or entities subject to a specific license condition requiring audited financial statements. A marine claims surveyor without public investment or banking/insurance licensure falls outside mandatory audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Business Corporations Act does not prescribe a mandatory GAAP or IFRS framework. Financial records must be sufficient to present an accurate financial condition and support the preparation of financial statements; IFRS or US GAAP may be adopted voluntarily. Non-resident tax-exempt entities typically use IFRS for internal reporting and any contractual or lender requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public UBO register exists in the Marshall Islands. Under the Business Corporations Act and the Registered Agent Regulations, the licensed registered agent must collect and confirm beneficial ownership particulars annually as part of anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance. Any transfer of shares that changes beneficial ownership must be reported to the registered agent within 30 days of the transfer, and the agent must update its electronic and physical records; a confirmation statement is maintained by the agent, not filed with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000 – $15,000 USD per year (only if voluntarily commissioned or imposed by contractual lender)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — non-resident domestic Business Corporation (MH_BC) is fully exempt from Marshall Islands income tax on foreign-source income; a 3% gross revenue tax applies exclusively to gross revenues derived from sources within the Marshall Islands (Income Tax Act 1989, Title 54, Section 179).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Complete tax exemption for non-resident-owned non-resident domestic corporations on non-RMI-source income; no capital gains tax; no branch remittance tax; no dividend distribution tax. Marine insurance surveying fees earned entirely outside RMI territorial waters and from non-RMI-flagged vessels are outside the gross revenue tax base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Annual Corporate Statement (Statement of Status) and Annual Fee — Business Corporations Act 1990, Section 121; filed through the RMI Registrar of Corporations online portal via a licensed RMI Registered Agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation; no fiscal year-end income tax return is required for a non-resident exempt corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the Business Corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation, including the 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' suffix.
Use the number assigned by the Registrar; verify on the current annual fee invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, including number of shares and par value or statement of no par value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State authorized capital in United States Dollars as per the articles of incorporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of shares issued and outstanding as of the filing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only shares actually issued; a non-resident BC may have one or more non-resident individual or corporate shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address and mailing address of the registered office in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the registered agent's street address in Majuro or Ebeye; a PO Box alone is insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and address of the licensed RMI registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed registered agent in good standing with the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and residential or business addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural persons or entities may serve; disclose all directors and the incumbent officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer as applicable).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the corporation is a resident or non-resident domestic corporation for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm non-resident status and certify the absence of income derived from RMI sources to maintain the zero-tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of the annual fee incurs a statutory surcharge of 10% per month or part of a month on the unpaid balance; failure to file or pay for three consecutive years leads to administrative dissolution by the Registrar; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, a reinstatement fee, and a late filing penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Gross Revenue Tax Return for Corporations (Form RMI-C) — RMI Income Tax Division, Ministry of Finance; electronically filed via the RMI Online Tax Portal or by paper submission to the Income Tax Division, Majuro.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly prepayments only if RMI-source gross revenue exceeds statutory thresholds)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the corporate fiscal year (April 15 for calendar-year corporations); a non-resident exempt corporation with no RMI-source revenue has no filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I - Gross Revenue from RMI Sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue received or accrued from sources within the Marshall Islands, including surveying services performed in RMI territory or on RMI-flagged vessels with RMI-source maritime activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 if all marine survey fees are earned outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands from non-RMI sources; attach a short statement describing the foreign-source basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of statutory exemptions relied upon to reduce or eliminate gross revenue tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cite the non-resident domestic corporation exemption and the absence of income tax treaty or concession; list exempt foreign-source survey contract revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of gross revenue tax at the 3% statutory rate on RMI-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a fully non-resident exempt corporation, the amount due is $0.00; do not compute tax on foreign-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part IV - Officer Declaration and Signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed certification under penalty of perjury that the return and accompanying statements are true and complete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any officer or director may sign; if no return is required, maintain the signed annual statement in the corporate minute book.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment penalties accrue at 5% per month of the unpaid gross revenue tax, capped at 25%; interest accrues at the statutory rate; willful failure to file or tax evasion may result in criminal fines up to $10,000 and imprisonment for up to 3 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions declared by a Business Corporation to its shareholders, whether resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable — the Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network and does not issue tax residency certificates for treaty relief. Where a foreign payor jurisdiction imposes withholding tax on dividends paid by an MH_BC, the protocol is: (1) obtain a certificate of non-residence or tax exemption letter from the RMI Registrar of Corporations addressed to the payor's tax administration; (2) provide the foreign payor with the RMI Certificate of Incorporation and current Statement of Status; (3) rely on the payor jurisdiction's unilateral foreign-source dividend exemption or applicable domestic law. No RMI withholding tax application form exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% for royalties and interest paid by an RMI Business Corporation to non-residents; the RMI levies no withholding tax on cross-border interest or intellectual property royalties. Treaty: Not applicable — no DTA partner countries; effective foreign tax risk depends entirely on the recipient's residence jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — the Marshall Islands imposes no transfer pricing documentation regime and has no local file or master file thresholds; the RMI gross revenue tax operates on a gross receipts basis with no arm's length adjustment mechanism. Prudent practice: for intercompany contracts with affiliated underwriters, maintain contemporaneous commercial agreements, fee schedules, and survey reports demonstrating arm's length fee levels, even though no statutory documentation threshold applies.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are currently in force in the Marshall Islands for foreign-owned non-resident corporations, and the RMI is not listed on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions. However, an MH_BC engaged in marine insurance surveying must maintain minimum substance: a licensed RMI registered agent, a physical registered office in Majuro or Ebeye, current annual corporate statement filings, and actual operational records (contracts, claims inspection reports, vessel survey logs, and bank account statements) sufficient to rebut any inference of being a shell company by counterparty banks, underwriters, or foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully concealing RMI-source gross revenue, falsely declaring non-resident exempt status while performing marine survey or claims inspection services in RMI territorial waters or on RMI-flagged vessels generating RMI-source income, or submitting a false annual statement to the Registrar or Income Tax Division.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fraud penalty of 50% of the underpaid gross revenue tax plus statutory interest at the prescribed annual rate; criminal fine up to $10,000 and imprisonment for up to 3 years under the RMI Income Tax Act 1989; forfeiture of any unlawful tax benefit claimed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or knowingly cause concealment of income are jointly and severally liable for civil fraud penalties and may be subject to criminal prosecution, travel bans, and asset freezing orders issued by the RMI High Court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Non-Filing and Administrative Dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual corporate statement or pay the annual fee for three consecutive years; maintaining an empty corporate vehicle with no bank account, no business records, and no commercial substance despite active marine claims inspection operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution by the Registrar of Corporations; loss of corporate name and good standing; contracts and legal actions by the dissolved corporation become voidable; reinstatement requires payment of all current and accrued annual fees, a 10% monthly late surcharge, a reinstatement fee, and re-registration formalities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: After dissolution, directors who continue to transact business in the name of the dissolved corporation incur personal liability for all resulting debts under BCA Section 122; courts will pierce the corporate veil and impose civil restitution of any fees collected from underwriters.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to establish or update the RMI Beneficial Ownership Register, failing to report changes in beneficial ownership to the registered agent within required timeframes, or knowingly processing premium or claims settlement payments connected to marine insurance fraud, sanctions evasion, or tainted cargo claims through payment rails such as Underwriter Wire or Wise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate monetary penalties under the RMI AML/CTF framework and Banking Act of up to $150,000 per violation; inclusion of the entity on financial institution risk lists; freezing of bank accounts; potential suspension or revocation of the corporation's existence for deliberate disregard of AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face criminal fines up to $50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for predicate money laundering offenses; courts may impose personal disqualification from serving as directors or officers of any RMI entity and issue travel restrictions pending resolution of enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Rendering marine cargo or hull claims inspection and survey services within the Republic of the Marshall Islands or on behalf of RMI-domestic underwriters without the required business license and any applicable maritime surveyor authorization; issuing survey certificates without statutory liability insurance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cessation orders and monetary fines under the RMI Business License Act; administrative nullification of survey certificates issued without a license; denial of evidentiary weight to such certificates in RMI insurance claims litigation; suspension of good standing status until the appropriate license is obtained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly conduct unlicensed surveying operations are personally liable for restitution of all fees collected, litigation costs, and legal damages arising from invalidated survey reports; criminal charges may trigger bail conditions, international travel bans, and, upon conviction, disqualification from professional practice in the maritime sector.
